next_step: POC kickoff on hosted API; define prompt parity suite and baseline tests
notes: Summary: Emberfall is a mid-market UX/product analytics SaaS evaluating Redwood to replace an existing LLM API provider for multiple features (agent support, doc search, summarization, code-assist). Primary goal: move quickly on Hosted API POC, validate prompt parity, then migrate to Dedicated for predictable throughput and lower unit cost.

Background: currently on legacy provider (OpenAI) for embeddings + chat. CTO wants vendor diversification and better cost controls; engineering team worried about regressions in summarization and hallucination rates.
Decision makers: CTO (L. Grant), Head of Product (S. Morales), Lead ML Engineer (K. Chen). AE engaged with Jordan Patel; SE support by Maya Rodriguez.

Technical requirements: target average chat latency <= 200ms p50, p95 <= 700ms for 1k token responses; embedding throughput ~120 reqs/min at peak; support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints or easy compat layer; KV cache for session state; SAML SSO + SOC2 required for procurement.
POC plan (agreed in call 2026-03-08):
- Phase 1 (2 weeks, Hosted): smoke test endpoints, run ~2000 prompts across 4 prompt families, collect metrics: latency, token cost, toxicity/regression signals.

- Phase 2 (2 weeks): parity evaluation — automated prompt suite (see Drive: prompt-parity-suite.xlsx). pass threshold: no more than 5% delta on core QA metrics, and <3% increase in hallucination for summaries.
- Phase 3 (4 weeks): Dedicated trial (reserved pool) — run canary traffic, measure tail latency and cost per 1k tokens; validate autoscaling and fallback behavior between model variants.
Notes from last meeting (FF-2026-03-08-5091):
- "We need a compatibility layer so engineers don't rewrite the whole client." quoted from Lead ML Eng K. Chen.
- Maya demoed Redwood Hosted API compatibility mode; engineering liked the OpenAI-compat endpoints but requested clearer mapping doc for streaming and function calling edge cases.
- Legal flagged potential contract change: data retention and log access during POC — needs SLM from Redwood legal (Jordan to escalate).
Migration concerns called out by engineering:
- Prompt parity: templated prompts behave slightly different under different tokenizers; need a systematic approach to detect regressions.
- Regression tracking: want nightly evals, baseline test harness; Redwood Optimize suggestions are attractive but want proof.

Commercial: Emberfall is cost-sensitive — looking for pricing that beats or matches current unit cost at 100M tokens/month projection. Interested in committed reserved capacity discounts for Dedicated.
Operational ask: must support VPC peering for Dedicated and option to keep PII vectors in customer-managed key store (KMS).
Next steps (short):
- Jordan to schedule POC kickoff 2026-03-15 (hosted API).
- Maya to share prompt parity checklist + initial baseline scripts by 2026-03-12 (Drive link).
- Engineering to provide sample prompt families and eval metrics by 2026-03-13.
Open questions / risks:
- How to quantify "parity" for reranking pipelines — Emberfall uses reranker + embedding scoring; want guidance on compatibility and degradations.
- If Hosted POC shows >5% regression on critical metrics, migration to Dedicated may be delayed and require model tuning with Redwood Research.
Call artifacts: Fireflies transcript IDs above, PRD + pricing deck in drive. Jira tickets RDW-1423 (SAML onboarding) and RDW-1509 (compat layer mapping) opened for tracking.
